ds: Terrorist supporters may solicit and move small to moderate amounts through virtual assets, using self-hosted wallets, privacy-enhanced assets, mixers or decentralised services. Risks are driven by pseudonymity and cross-border speed, balanced against traceability on public blockchains.

src.t: FATF, Targeted Update on Implementation of the FATF Standards on Virtual Assets and VASPs (annual since 2019)
FATF, Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers (2021)

cn.rt: Customers send small amounts from everyday accounts to exchanges and self-hosted wallets via remote channels.

rat: Self-hosted wallets, mixers, P2P exchanges, fiat on and off-ramps.

ind.n: Deposits from or withdrawals to wallets attributed to terrorist fundraising
ind.cx: On-chain analytics link counterparty addresses to published designations or documented fundraising campaigns.
ind.fp: Attribution can be incorrect or outdated; shared services create indirect exposure.
ind.ds: Customer transacts directly or near-directly with blockchain addresses attributed by sanctions lists or analytics to designated persons, thefts, ransomware or terrorist fundraising.
ind.cn: Exposure to wallets attributed to designated, stolen-fund or illicit actors

ind.n: Retail users with repeated small transfers to many new addresses
ind.cx: Frequent low-value outbound transfers to different external wallets after small incoming crowd-sourced payments.
ind.fp: Tipping, gaming and DeFi use produce similar patterns.
ind.ds: Repeated small or fixed-amount transfers to many fresh or new crypto addresses.
ind.cn: Transfers to many newly created crypto addresses

ind.n: Use of privacy coins or mixing services with higher-risk geographies
ind.cx: Conversion to privacy-enhanced assets or routing through mixers, paired with geographic indicators.
ind.fp: Privacy preference is lawful for many users.
ind.ds: Funds are moved through mixers, privacy coins or rapid cross-chain conversion to obscure origin.
ind.cn: Use of mixers, chain-hopping or privacy coins

ind.n: Customer location inconsistent with declared residence
ind.cx: IP or device signals suggest access from conflict-adjacent regions while KYC indicates elsewhere.
ind.fp: Travel, expatriates and VPNs cause mismatches.
ind.ds: IP or device signals suggest access from conflict-adjacent regions while KYC indicates elsewhere.

ind.n: Solicitation of donations via social channels using addresses linked to extremist content
ind.cx: Publicly advertised wallet addresses appear in extremist channels or campaigns.
ind.ds: Publicly advertised wallet addresses appear in extremist channels or campaigns.

ind.n: Rapid conversion of donations to stablecoins then off-ramp through peer-to-peer channels
ind.cx: Funds are converted and cashed out using unregulated peer-to-peer exchanges.
ind.fp: P2P trading is a common legitimate on-ramp in some regions.
ind.ds: Funds are converted and cashed out using unregulated peer-to-peer exchanges.

ind.n: Onboarding with weak identity evidence and shared devices
ind.cx: Multiple accounts opened with synthetic or inconsistent identity data from common devices.
ind.fp: Households and shared devices are common.
ind.ds: Identity documents, contact details, geolocation or device data do not align, suggesting fabricated, stolen or misrepresented identity.
ind.cn: Inconsistent or synthetic identity data at onboarding

ind.n: Sudden large inflows from newly funded unhosted wallets
ind.cx: Large first deposits from unhosted wallets with no history, followed by immediate transfers out.
ind.fp: Users migrating between platforms behave this way.
ind.ds: Large first deposits from unhosted wallets with no history, followed by immediate transfers out.

ctl.ds: Traces exposure of deposit and withdrawal addresses to illicit clusters and screens wallets with risk-scored alerts. It reveals on-chain exposure.

ctl.n: Funds hold, freeze and recall procedure
ctl.ds: Provides a defined, legally grounded capability to restrict, hold, freeze or recall funds and accounts pending review or on confirmed exposure, with clear triggers and approvers. It stops onward dissipation of suspected illicit funds.
Flags direct and indirect exposure to mixers, privacy services and obfuscation tools against defined thresholds and applies enhanced review. It manages the traceability loss these tools create.

ctl.n: Fan-in, fan-out and funnel account detection
ctl.ds: Detects accounts receiving from many unrelated senders, or sending to many beneficiaries, followed by consolidation or onward movement. It surfaces collector, funnel and mule structures.

Collects, validates and transmits required originator and beneficiary information with virtual asset transfers and holds or blocks transfers where counterparty data is missing or unreliable. It brings wire-like transparency to virtual asset payments.

ctl.n: Risk appetite and product policy statements
ctl.ds: Documents the institution's appetite and permitted or prohibited products, assets and activities for a given risk area, with limits and review cadence. It gives staff and systems a clear boundary for acceptance.

Detects use of VPN, proxy and anonymising services and compares access geolocation with declared residence and sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions. It reveals concealed location and supports geographic restrictions.
Requires phishing-resistant authentication and additional verification on risky sessions, credential or payee changes and large payments. It blocks unauthorised access and payments.
Participates in sector, regulator and public-private forums and platform cooperation to receive and share typologies and indicators where lawful. It keeps scenarios current.
Alerts when inflows are quickly moved out with little retained balance, including cash-in fast-out and rapid conversion or cash-out. It reveals accounts used as conduits for layering.

Caps transaction size, frequency, load, withdrawal and deposit values, with staged increases as legitimate behaviour is established and per-customer limits at kiosks. It bounds the loss and laundering capacity of new or higher-risk accounts.

Fingerprints devices, IP addresses, emulators and network attributes to link applications, sessions and accounts and to flag shared or anomalous infrastructure. It exposes mule rings and multiple-account abuse.

Applies enhanced review, approval, limits and conditions to relationships or flows that involve jurisdictions rated higher risk for secrecy, corruption, conflict or weak controls. Triggers include nationality, residence, counterparties and payment routing.

Requires proof of control, such as a signed message or small test transfer, before large transfers to or from privately held wallets are accepted. It confirms the customer owns the wallet and prevents use of third-party or hostile-controlled addresses.
